title: Deep Learning
authors: Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio & Aaron Courville
note: Read chapters 2–5 for math and probability, then connect networks, regularization, and optimization in chapters 6–8.

title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
note: Write out the first and second moment updates and bias correction, then explain how Adam differs from SGD.

title: PyTorch: Learn the Basics
note: Follow the complete workflow: tensors, DataLoader, autograd, training loops, and saving models.

title: PyTorch: Automatic Mixed Precision
note: Add autocast and GradScaler to your training loop, then measure speed and GPU memory use.

title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
note: Understand residual mappings in ResNet, then check tensor shapes and gradient paths across skip connections.

title: Layer Normalization
authors: Jimmy Lei Ba, Jamie Ryan Kiros & Geoffrey E. Hinton
note: Mark the dimensions used for normalization and compare the statistics in LayerNorm and BatchNorm.

title: Attention Is All You Need
note: Work through Q/K/V, the scaling factor, multi-head attention, and the FFN, labeling every tensor shape.

title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
note: Understand RoPE through 2D rotations and derive how relative position enters the Q–K dot product.

title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
note: Distinguish arithmetic complexity from GPU memory I/O, and explain how tiling and recomputation reduce memory costs.

title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
note: Trace the data, normalization, positional encoding, and pretraining pipeline of a decoder-only model.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
note: Read the curves for model size, dataset size, and compute budget, then discuss the limits of these empirical laws.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
note: Derive the parameter count of a low-rank update, implement a LoRA linear layer, and compare ranks and target layers.

title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
note: Separate frozen quantized weights from trainable adapters, and understand NF4, double quantization, and memory use.

title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
authors: William Fedus, Barret Zoph & Noam Shazeer
note: Understand top-1 routing, capacity limits, and load balancing; use routing histograms to check for expert collapse.

title: Mixtral of Experts
note: Compare sparse experts with dense FFNs, and explain total parameters, active parameters, and compute costs.

title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
note: Start with patch embeddings and trace ViT's sequence length, CLS token, and positional encodings.

title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
note: Write out CLIP's bidirectional contrastive loss and explain how text prompts enable zero-shot classification.

title: Emerging Properties in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers
note: Compare DINO's self-distillation objective with CLIP's image–text alignment, and explore uses for patch features.

title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
note: Derive the VAE's ELBO and explain how reparameterization enables backpropagation through stochastic latent variables.

title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
authors: Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain & Pieter Abbeel
note: Connect the forward noising process, noise prediction loss, and reverse sampling; plot a noise schedule yourself.

title: Flow Matching for Generative Modeling
note: Use a 2D toy distribution to understand probability paths, velocity field regression, and ODE sampling.

title: Visual Instruction Tuning
note: Draw LLaVA's vision encoder → projector → LLM pipeline, and distinguish alignment from instruction tuning.

title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models
note: Understand how Q-Former queries connect a frozen vision encoder with a frozen language model.

title: Qwen2.5-VL Technical Report
note: Focus on dynamic resolution, visual tokens, and temporal encoding; trace the path from an image to an answer.

title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
authors: Geoffrey Hinton, Oriol Vinyals & Jeff Dean
note: Understand soft targets and temperature, write the distillation loss, and explain the teacher and student roles.

title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
note: Understand how outliers affect quantization error, and report accuracy, inference latency, and peak GPU memory.

title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
note: Plot PPO's clipped objective and explain the probability ratio, advantage, and limits on policy updates.

title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
note: Build intuition for the DPO loss from preference pairs, explain the reference policy, and compare the workflow with RLHF.

title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
note: Trace the training signals through InstructGPT's SFT, preference data, reward modeling, and PPO stages.

title: MovieChat: From Dense Token to Sparse Memory for Long Video Understanding
note: Compare short-term and long-term memory designs, and discuss what information video token compression may lose.

title: MA-LMM: Memory-Augmented Large Multimodal Model for Long-Term Video Understanding
note: Trace memory bank updates during online processing, and compare accuracy and cost under a fixed memory budget.

title: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion
note: Understand conditional diffusion over action sequences, receding horizon control, and closed-loop replanning.

title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control
note: Explain how robot actions become tokens and how training combines image–text tasks with robot trajectories.

title: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models
note: Understand DreamerV3's latent dynamics and imagined rollouts, then discuss how model errors propagate.

title: How to Read a Paper
note: Use the three-pass method; record each paper's problem, method, evidence, assumptions, and open questions.

title: Improving Reproducibility in Machine Learning Research (A Report from the NeurIPS 2019 Reproducibility Program)
note: Create a reproducibility checklist covering data splits, random seeds, hyperparameters, and compute budget.
